 Steady progress: Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing have reached two finals – the China Masters last month and the French Open last Sunday in just six months together. 
 PETALING JAYA: Every win brings with it increased attention and expectations, but professional mixed doubles shuttler Hoo Pang Ron is looking to learn from every game instead.
 The 28-year-old and his partner Lai Pei Jing, 34, have enjoyed a remarkable October, reaching the semi-finals of the Denmark Open two weeks ago before finishing runners-up at the French Open last Sunday.
 Their strong performances have propelled them from 51st to 24th in the world rankings, raising expectations ahead of their Hylo Open campaign, which begins today in Saarbrucken, Germany.
 However, Pang Ron, who turned independent in April, is determined not to let their hot streak distract him from the bigger picture.
 “Every match is important. We are always learning,” said Pang Ron.
 “We just go step by step and never give ourselves too much pressure.
 “But of course, this run of form boosts our confidence.”
 In just six months together, Pang Ron-Pei Jing have already reached two finals – the China Masters last month and the French Open last Sunday.
 Although they fell short against Chinese world No. 1 Feng Yanzhe-Huang Dongping on both occasions, Pang Ron believes the experience has helped him grow as a player.
 “Personally, I feel I’ve learnt how to enjoy and control my emotions a little better.”
 Pang Ron is also mindful of the pressure that comes with being viewed as potential title contenders.
 The absence of Yanzhe-Dongping in Germany presents an opportunity for Pang Ron to end his seven-year title drought. His last triumph came at the 2019 Hyderabad Open alongside former partner Cheah Yee See.
 Nevertheless, Pang Ron is refusing to get carried away.
 “The draw won’t be easy as we’re not seeded.”
 While the added attention brings heightened expectations, it has also opened doors for him in attracting greater interest from potential sponsors.
 “Hopefully I can continue to impress. It’s not easy covering all the expenses as an independent player.”
